receipt.public_excerpt: Such "hallucinations" persist even in state-of-the-art systems and undermine trust.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper supports concern about existing systems. Its explanation depends on training and evaluation incentives and does not establish that every future LLM must retain the same problem.

This conditional theoretical result challenges the inference from mathematical inevitability to practical untrustworthiness. It neither demonstrates zero hallucinations in a deployed model nor guarantees that its data assumptions can be met.

The authors report zero hallucinations in an evaluation of 70 academic prompts conducted in February 2025. This is material counterevidence to a claim that hallucinations must occur in every evaluation, but it does not establish elimination of the underlying propensity.

unresolved_gaps: No independently validated general-purpose counterexample with a guarantee against hallucinations was established.
The theoretical results have assumptions that do not settle the unrestricted claim about all future LLMs.
The claim supplies no threshold for when residual errors make an output untrustworthy.
